chunks: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ghalib from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu al-Subah Sabih ibn Abdillah from Sabbar, the mawla of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who fasts for twenty-nine days and breaks his fast due to the sighting [of the moon], then fasts again due to the sighting; does he make up one day? He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: No, unless two just witnesses come and testify that they saw it [the moon] the night before, in which case he makes up one day.'

key_terms.لِلرُّؤْيَةِ: due to the sighting [of the moon]

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up a day if one breaks the fast for moon sighting and then resumes fasting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of lunar sighting (*ru'yah*) in Shia fiqh, specifically addressing the scenario where a month is completed in twenty-nine days based on testimony but later confirmed as thirty. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that a make-up day (*qada*) is only obligatory if two just witnesses testify to having seen the crescent the night before the initial break, highlighting the Shia reliance on credible witness testimony over mere astronomical calculation for determining the start and end of Ramadan.
